plan_a_advantages: Includes longer, more challenging trail runs that directly address the goal of speed.
Provides a more balanced approach to building aerobic fitness with a mix of easy and moderate intensity sessions.
The longer runs (75-90 minutes) are more representative of typical trail race distances.
plan_b_advantages: Features a cross-training session, which can be beneficial for injury prevention and overall fitness.
Has more rest days, potentially useful for an athlete who is new to training or recovering from an injury.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, moderate-intensity trail runs (60-90 minutes) which are crucial for building the aerobic base necessary for faster trail running. Plan B, while seemingly gentler with shorter runs and more rest days, lacks the sustained aerobic stimulus required for significant speed improvements. Plan A’s structure allows for a gradual increase in volume, building endurance without excessive fatigue, which is key for a runner looking to improve their pace.
